0.long_answer: The enzyme is α-N-acetylgalactosaminidase, also known as Nagalase. In cancer patients, this enzyme accumulates in the serum, and its activity correlates with tumor burden and aggressiveness. In contrast, individuals with Schindler disease have a deficiency of this enzyme due to mutations affecting its production or activity. As such, α-N-acetylgalactosaminidase plays a critical role both as a marker in cancer and in the pathogenesis of Schindler disease.
